entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Juan Rodríguez de Fonseca (1451–1524) was a Spanish archbishop, a courtier and bureaucrat, whose position as royal chaplain to Queen Isabella enabled him to become a powerful counsellor to Ferdinand and Isabella, the Catholic Monarchs. He controlled the Casa de Contratación, an agency which managed expeditions to the New World on behalf of the Spanish crown. He later served as the president of the Council of the Indies, when it was founded in 1521. He managed the administration of a number of significant Spanish expeditions including voyages by Christopher Columbus and Magellan's circumnavigation of the earth.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Juan Rodríguez de Fonseca played a crucial role in shaping Spanish exploration and colonization of the New World through his leadership of expeditions led by Christopher Columbus and Ferdinand Magellan. His administration of these expeditions had significant consequences for the course of world history.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Juan Rodríguez de Fonseca played a crucial role in shaping Spain's New World expansion through his leadership of expeditions and administration of the Casa de Contratación. His involvement with Ferdinand and Isabella, as well as Christopher Columbus and Magellan, had significant regional impact on Spanish colonization.
